rules.title: Hoboken Rent Control - Hardship Increase Procedure and Exemptions
rules.requirement: Landlords may apply to the Rent Leveling and Stabilization Board for a hardship rent increase based on factors like management quality, prudent investment, and reasonable operating expenses; tenants may likewise apply for a rent decrease if services decline. Newly constructed dwellings and buildings vacant since January 1, 1984 may qualify for exemption from rent control as determined by the Rent Regulation Officer.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to dwellings subject to Hoboken's rent control ordinance; exemptions available for newly constructed dwellings and buildings vacant since January 1, 1984.
rules.exemptions: Newly constructed dwellings; buildings completely vacant since January 1, 1984.
rules.quoted_span: The Rent Regulation Officer shall make all determinations regarding the eligibility of a building completely vacant since January 1, 1984, for an exemption as defined above.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the building is newly constructed or was vacant since January 1, 1984 (affects rent control exemption eligibility)

rules.conflict_note: This chunk only describes procedural hardship-increase criteria and exemption determinations; the numeric rent increase cap itself is not stated in this excerpt and appears elsewhere in the ordinance.
